The move comes as Canada faces criticism from Donald Trump’s administration over its “unacceptable” efforts to combat forced labour.

Two helicopters collided over Rio de Janeiro on Sunday morning and crashed in the city’s western zone, killing all six people onboard, including Tree, several Brazilian media outlets reported.

guardian.description:

Half of the world’s children are exposed to at least three overlapping climate hazards threatening their health, education and survival, according to a Unicef report.

Globally, children face increasing threats from heatwaves, storms, floods and droughts as the climate crisis worsens, with more than one billion facing at least three of these at once.

rfi.title: Child sexual abuse commission urges France to speed up reforms
rfi.description: Only a third of the recommendations made more than two years ago by France's Independent Commission on Incest and Sexual Violence Against Children (Ciivise) have been fully implemented, the body said in an assessment submitted to the government.

rfi.title: Journalists disappear as intimidation grips Mozambique's Cabo Delgado region
rfi.description: Almost a decade after an Islamist insurgency erupted in Mozambique's northern Cabo Delgado province, few reports on the conflict are emerging from the region. This third instalment of Mozambique Exposed – an investigation coordinated by Forbidden Stories, to which RFI contributed – hears from journalists and activists facing intimidation and violence.

rfi.title: France's Macron warns Iran against imposing Hormuz tolls
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday warned Iran against imposing tolls on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, saying "everything" should be done so fees are not charged for passage through the key bottleneck.

rfi.title: US and Iran reach deal to end war, reopen Hormuz
rfi.description: The United States and Iran said they reached a deal to end the Middle East war on all fronts including Lebanon, and reopen the vital Strait of Hormuz, but offered little indication on the thorny question of Tehran's nuclear programme.

rfi.title: NGO warns Ebola epidemic is 'outpacing' response efforts in DRC
rfi.description: French NGO Doctors Without Borders warned Monday that "dangerous gaps" remain in efforts to rein in an Ebola outbreak that has killed more than 180 people in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Since the first reported cases a month ago, the virus has spread rapidly, with the situation now critical in Ituri province.

rfi.title: ‘No blank cheque' for president or government says Senegal’s Sonko
rfi.description: In his first major international interview since becoming Speaker of Senegal's National Assembly, former prime minister Ousmane Sonko talks to RFI and sister channel France 24 about his split with his long-time ally President Bassirou Diomaye Faye. In the wide-reaching discussion, he also touches on the debt crisis, homosexuality legislation, regional security, his political aspirations and the World Cup.

rfi.title: First contact: Cape Verde's rise to the global stage
rfi.description: Cape Verde will make its World Cup debut at the 2026 tournament in the United States, Mexico and Canada. In the third instalment of a four-part series, RFI looks at the journey of the second smallest nation after Curaçao to qualify for the competition in its 96-year history.

rfi.title: Macron leads effort to bridge divides with Trump at France's G7 summit
rfi.description: As a G7 summit opens in eastern France on Monday, President Emmanuel Macron is set to lead the allies' efforts to narrow differences with the United States on Iran, Ukraine, trade and big tech regulation.

rfi.title: Cameroon opposition figure files complaint in France against President Biya
rfi.description: Former Cameroonian presidential candidate Issa Tchiroma Bakary says he's filed two complaints with the Paris Judicial Court against President Paul Biya, citing the principle of universal jurisdiction.

rfi.title: Clashes as thousands protest in Geneva ahead of G7 summit in France
rfi.description: Protesters in Geneva threw stones and firecrackers at the police, who responded with tear gas and water cannons during a demonstration Sunday against the G7 summit in nearby Evian.

rfi.title: Somaliland president makes 'historic' visit to Israel
rfi.description: Somaliland's President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi met his Israeli counterpart on Sunday in Jerusalem in his first-ever state visit, which comes months after Israel officially recognised the breakaway African state.

rfi.title: UK intercepts Russian shadow fleet vessel in Channel: ministry
rfi.description: British forces on Sunday intercepted a sanctioned oil tanker belonging to Russia's shadow fleet in the English Channel, the defence ministry said, in a six-hour operation hailed by Kyiv.

rfi.title: The project nurturing West Africa's new generation of women filmmakers
rfi.description: Some of the West African film industry's biggest names are backing a new mentorship programme to support emerging women filmmakers. Showcased at this year's Cannes Film Festival, the Mariama Lab project aims to help women bring their stories to a wider audience in the region and beyond.

rfi.title: Ghana lodges protest over Canada's refusal to admit rape case suspect Partey
rfi.description: Ghana's government confirmed on Saturday it had lodged a formal protest with Canada over its refusal to issue an entry visa to the Ghana midfielder Thomas Partey ahead of Ghana's game against Panama on Wednesday in Toronto.

rfi.title: South Africa accused of failing to crack down on anti-immigrant violence
rfi.description: Several African countries are repatriating their citizens from South Africa following weeks of xenophobic attacks on black migrants. The vigilante violence has drawn international condemnation, with some accusing the South African authorities of failing to take a tough approach.

rfi.title: Whistleblowing is on the rise in France, but expert says support remains lacking
rfi.description: Whistleblowing in France is on the rise, according to the independent authority in charge of protecting those who speak out in the public interest. The Défenseur des Droits has seen an increase in cases, reflecting a growing awareness of the process of speaking out and the protection available for those who do.

rfi.title: Resumption of $20bn Cabo Delgado gas project reignites both hope and resentment
rfi.description: The resumption of one of the world's biggest gas projects by French energy giant TotalEnergies, after a five-year suspension following a deadly jihadist attack, has raised hopes of jobs and prosperity in northern Mozambique. But this second instalment of Mozambique Exposed – an investigation coordinated by Forbidden Stories, to which RFI contributed – questions whether the country's vast gas wealth will benefit local communities.

rfi.title: Six Georgians jailed for theft of rare Russian books in France
rfi.description: Six Georgians have been sentenced to up to seven years' jail in France over the theft of rare editions of Russian literary classics, including by 19th-century luminary Alexander Pushkin, from prestigious French libraries.

euronews.title: On the Pont Neuf, artist JR's 'Caverne' opens to the public
euronews.description: Open until 28 June, JR’s latest art installation, by the master of XXL photographs, whisks pedestrians in central Paris into the depths of a cave.

euronews.title: WATCH: Bolton says Trump played like violin by Iran
euronews.description: Iran outmanoeuvred US President Donald Trump "like a violin" in negotiations, walking away with far better terms after sensing his desperation for a deal to end the war, former National Security Adviser John Bolton told Euronews.

euronews.title: €31bn drug trade, 7,600 deaths: How the EU plans to tackle the drug crisis
euronews.description: 29 million Europeans use drugs every year, and the market has an estimated €31 billion value. The European Council has released a new framework to completely change how the EU handles this enormous problem, from enforcement to public health.

euronews.title: Protesting and cheering as Iran's World Cup match divides diaspora
euronews.description: Iran's opening World Cup match drew both supporters and protesters outside the stadium near Los Angeles, highlighting divisions within the Iranian-American community.

euronews.title: Eight killed in US Air Force B-52 bomber crash in California
euronews.description: Eight people were killed when a B-52 bomber crashed and burst into flames shortly after takeoff from Edwards Air Force Base in Southern California. Officials said the aircraft was on a routine test mission and the cause remains under investigation.

euronews.title: Iran 'played Trump like a violin' in deal, former national security adviser Bolton tells Euronews
euronews.description: Bolton tells Euronews the US sacrificed its strategic leverage as Trump prioritised lowering oil prices, while Iran walks away with the deal it wanted.

euronews.title: G7 summit: Zelenskyy joins leaders to discuss revival of peace talks
euronews.description: The second day of the G7 summit in Évian, France, is underway. Russia's war on Ukraine is the first item on the agenda.

euronews.title: Bank of Japan raises its key interest rate to a three-decade high
euronews.description: The Bank of Japan raised its benchmark interest rate to 1% on Tuesday, citing challenges stemming from a weak Japanese yen and higher prices.

euronews.title: Bonnie Tyler out of induced coma but still in serious condition
euronews.description: The 75-year-old Welsh singer has been in intensive care at Faro Hospital since early May following emergency surgery for a perforated bowel.

euronews.title: Europe Today: Inside the G7 Summit in Évian
euronews.description: Global leaders are gathering in the French spa town of Évian les Bains for the second day of the G7. US President Donald Trump told allies that he expects the Strait of Hormuz to be “fully open” on Friday, where the framework deal to end the war is expected to be formalised in Switzerland.

euronews.title: Human skills increasingly in demand as AI reshapes labour market, PwC finds
euronews.description: As AI takes on more routine tasks, employers are placing a higher premium on judgment, creativity and leadership, according to a new PwC report.

euronews.title: Book a ‘Chef’s Table’ in business class: United upgrades dining on select long-haul flights
euronews.description: Ever wondered what happens when a streaming hit and an airline unite? US carrier United is collaborating with Netflix’s Chef’s Table to bring 30 new chef-curated dishes to its Polaris international business class.

euronews.description: The true extent of China's military AI remains unclear, despite public displays of autonomous drones, AI-powered naval weapons and "robot dogs," experts told Euronews.

euronews.title: World Cup 2026: Six million fans, three countries and a team racing to stop outbreaks
euronews.description: As six million fans travel across North America for the 2026 World Cup, health authorities are on alert for any sign of an infectious disease outbreak.

euronews.title: 6.7 magnitude earthquake strikes off of Indonesia, US Geological Survey says
euronews.description: Authorities have urged the public to heed official advice and instructions and exercise caution, warning that aftershocks can last hours.

euronews.title: Spain, Italy and France from the sea: inside one of the world's most popular cruises
euronews.description: The western Mediterranean is one of the world’s most popular cruise routes, drawing thousands who visit three top European destinations in a single trip without ever packing or unpacking.

euronews.title: Trump appears hesitant about ally-proposed plan to demine Strait of Hormuz for commercial traffic
euronews.description: Trump appeared hesitant to accept the European proposal, stressing that the strategic waterway will become open and safe thanks to his tentative deal to end the war with Iran, but remained open to the idea of some naval presence to ensure water safety for commercial passage.

lemonde.title: Accord Iran-Etats-Unis : à Téhéran, les conservateurs protestent, mais le cœur du pouvoir fait bloc
lemonde.description: Surnommée « les Inquiets », l’aile radicale du régime dénonce, y compris dans la rue, le protocole sur le cessez-le-feu et appelle à la vengeance contre Washington. Mais les gardiens de la révolution soutiennent l’accord que les autorités cherchent à présenter comme une victoire stratégique.

lemonde.title: L’invisibilité de Monique Barbut, symptôme de la disparition de l’écologie parmi les préoccupations au sommet de l’Etat
lemonde.description: La ministre de la transition écologique peine à s’imposer. Une situation qui dépasse sa seule personne et témoigne de l’abandon du sujet au sein du gouvernement.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, G7 à Evian : Volodymyr Zelensky est arrivé au sommet, où il doit s’entretenir avec Donald Trump
lemonde.description: Le président ukrainien participera à une réunion de travail - « Construire la paix et la sécurité pour l’Ukraine et l’Europe » - avant de rencontrer le président américain. La question du Moyen-Orient et de l’accord trouvé entre l’Iran et les Etats-Unis sera au cœur des discussions.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, bac 2026 : « Je passe la physique aujourd’hui, alors je prie pour que le sujet difficile tombe demain », découvrez les sujets après 9 heures
lemonde.description: Plus de 530 000 élèves de terminale générale et technologique plancheront, mardi 16 juin, sur leur première épreuve de spécialité au baccalauréat. Sujets, ressenti des candidats, éléments de corrigé… Suivez cette matinée d’épreuve avec nous.

lemonde.title: « Sur le terrain, c’est la catastrophe » : à Bunia, en RDC, face à une épidémie d’Ebola hors de contrôle
lemonde.description: Un mois après la déclaration officielle de l’épidémie par les autorités congolaises, la réponse sanitaire n’arrive pas à limiter la propagation du virus et le nombre de victimes ne fait qu’augmenter.

lemonde.title: Coupe du monde 2026 : ce qu’il faut retenir du lundi 15 juin et ce qu’il faudra suivre mardi 16
lemonde.description: Au lendemain de l’entrée ratée de l’Espagne, place à la France et à l’Argentine : les deux meilleures sélections de l’édition 2022 au Qatar entrent en lice, mardi, respectivement face au Sénégal et à l’Algérie.

lemonde.title: « Fait inédit, la campagne présidentielle se déroule sans règle préétablie ni arbitre pour la faire respecter »
lemonde.description: Hormis La France insoumise, déjà en ordre de bataille pour la présidentielle de 2027, aucun parti ni aucun camp n’échappe aux effets déstabilisateurs d’une recomposition politique loin d’être achevée, relève, dans sa chronique, Françoise Fressoz, éditorialiste au « Monde ».

lemonde.title: IA : le plan du gouvernement pour développer et réguler l’intelligence artificielle dans la fonction publique
lemonde.description: Le gouvernement a présenté, mardi, un « plan pour une IA utile, humaine et souveraine pour le service public ». Plusieurs outils vont être généralisés au sein de l’administration. Une « négociation sociale » sera aussi lancée, jeudi, pour encadrer l’usage de cette technologie.

lemonde.title: Banques en ligne : comment elles sont devenues incontournables
lemonde.description: Grâce à des tarifs plus faibles que ceux des réseaux historiques, les établissements numériques séduisent de plus en plus de clients, notamment les jeunes. Le marché se fragmente alors au profit de ces nouveaux venus.

lemonde.title: Le crash d’un bombardier B-52 sur une base militaire américaine en Californie fait huit morts
lemonde.description: L’accident s’est produit sur la base aérienne d’Edwards, lors d’un vol d’essai de routine, a fait savoir l’armée américaine.

lemonde.title: Des sirops de menthe trop verts : Yuka alerte contre le colorant bleu brillant FCF
lemonde.description: L’application dénonce la présence d’E133 dans une majorité des sirops de menthe, alors que ce colorant est suspecté de contribuer à certains troubles, notamment de l’attention. Elle demande aux industriels de généraliser les versions transparentes.

lemonde.title: En Suède, la culture du consensus piétinée par l’extrême droite
lemonde.description: A trois mois des législatives, prévues le 13 septembre, la pagaille règne dans les couloirs du Parlement, à Stockholm. En cause, la décision des élus du parti des Démocrates de Suède de rompre un pacte transpartisan qui permettait la bonne marche de l’Hémicycle.

lemonde.title: Bobbypills, l’irrévérencieux studio d’animation français derrière le film « Jim Queen »
lemonde.description: Son fondateur, David Alric, revient, avec le producteur Arthur Delabays et les coréalisateurs Marco Nguyen et Nicolas Athané, sur la difficile et longue genèse de cette comédie queer déjantée, projetée au Festival de Cannes.

lemonde.title: Brésil : les eaux amazoniennes retrouvent leur niveau après deux années de grave sécheresse
lemonde.description: Grâce à des précipitations importantes, les niveaux des rivières, des lacs et des plans d’eau d’Amazonie brésilienne ont été supérieurs, en 2025, de 2,6 % à la moyenne historique, d’après le réseau MapBiomas. Mais les chercheurs restent inquiets pour certains biomes, comme le Pantanal.

lemonde.title: Près de la moitié des enfants du monde sont exposés à au moins trois types d’aléas climatiques, alerte l’Unicef
lemonde.description: Au Tchad, pays en crise humanitaire, « plus de 95 % des enfants » sont menacés par la sécheresse, la chaleur extrême et la canicule, la combinaison la plus fréquente d’aléas climatiques dans le monde, selon l’agence onusienne.

lemonde.title: Les séries de la semaine : « House of the Dragon », « Everwood » et « Devil’s Playground »
lemonde.description: Chaque mardi, La Matinale du Monde propose une sélection de programmes à (re)découvrir sur petit écran. Aujourd’hui, notamment, la prévisible saison 3 des aventures de la dysfonctionnelle famille Targaryen.

france24fr.title: IA : la France va investir 655 millions d'euros supplémentaires pour accélérer sa "révolution"
france24fr.description: À la veille de l'ouverture du salon VivaTech, dédié aux nouvelles technologies, à Paris, le Premier ministre a annoncé mardi un investissement supplémentaire de 655 millions d'euros dans l’intelligence artificielle. Ces fonds doivent notamment renforcer les infrastructures, la recherche, les entreprises et les filières industrielles". L'objectif affiché est de soutenir la souveraineté technologique française et moderniser les services publics, afin "que cette révolution profite aux Français".

france24fr.title: France-Sénégal 2002 : le jour où les Lions de la Teranga ont fait tomber les champions du monde
france24fr.description: Pour la deuxième fois de leur histoire, la France et le Sénégal vont s'affronter mardi en Coupe du monde. Il y a 24 ans, les Lions de la Teranga avaient créé la sensation en Corée du Sud en battant les Bleus, champions du monde et d'Europe en titre.

france24fr.title: Accord entre les Etats-Unis et l'Iran: "Trump nous a trahis"
france24fr.description: A la Une de la presse, ce mardi 16 juin, la suite des réactions, aux Etats-Unis, à l’accord entre Washington et Téhéran pour mettre fin à la guerre en Iran. Un accord accueilli avec inquiétude au Liban et en Iran. Le combat d’une Franco-vietnamienne contre les multinationales responsables de l’épandage d’agent orange pendant la guerre du Vietnam. Le bel exploit du Cap-Vert face à l’Espagne au Mondial. Et la mobilisation en faveur de Christophe Gleizes.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Iran et Nouvelle-Zélande font match nul, bataille des symboles en tribunes
france24fr.description: Les équipes d'Iran et de Nouvelle-Zélande se sont neutralisées (2-2) lors de leur entrée en lice dans la Coupe du monde, lundi à Los Angeles. Des membres de la diaspora iranienne ont manifesté devant le stade, et de nombreux drapeaux ornés du lion et du soleil - symboles du drapeau avant la révolution de 1979 - ont été brandis dans les tribunes, notamment pendant l'hymne, en partie hué, avant que le public n'apporte un bruyant soutien aux joueurs.

france24fr.title: Antonio Guterres en visite de "solidarité" en Haïti
france24fr.description: Le secrétaire général de l'ONU Antonio Guterres est attendu mardi en Haïti pour exprimer sa "solidarité" avec les souffrances de la population. Plus de 5 000 personnes ont trouvé la mort en un an, victimes des violences liées aux gangs.

france24fr.title: En direct : les discussions sur un accord final avec Washington devraient débuter vendredi, selon Téhéran
france24fr.description: Les discussions sur un accord final avec les États-Unis devraient débuter vendredi, selon le chef de la diplomatie iranienne, Abbas Araghchi. De son côté, Donald Trump a affirmé lundi que le détroit d'Ormuz serait "complètement ouvert" vendredi. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Centrafrique : début du procès de l'ex-président François Bozizé pour crimes contre l'humanité
france24fr.description: La Cour pénale spéciale de Centrafrique ouvre le procès par contumace de l'ancien président François Bozizé. Âgé de 79 ans et exilé en Guinée-Bissau, il est accusé de crimes contre l’humanité commis entre 2009 et 2013 à Bossembélé. Meurtres, tortures, disparitions forcées et viols figurent parmi les crimes examinés par la justice.

france24fr.title: Au G7, un coup de projecteur attendu sur l'Ukraine en présence de Volodymyr Zelensky
france24fr.description: Volodymyr Zelensky est attendu mardi au G7 à Evian pour participer à une réunion de travail consacrée à la paix et la sécurité pour l'Ukraine et l'Europe. Il espère à cette occasion pouvoir s'entretenir seul à seul avec le président américain Donald Trump.

france24fr.title: Réseaux sociaux et plateformes vidéo dominent désormais le marché de l'information
france24fr.description: Davantage de personnes s'informent sur les réseaux sociaux et les plateformes vidéo que via les médias traditionnels, selon le rapport annuel de l'institut Reuters pour l'étude du journalisme publié mardi. C'est la première fois que ce mode de consommation de l'info est majoritaire sur la moyenne de l'ensemble des marchés étudiés.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : au courage, l'Arabie saoudite tient tête à l'Uruguay
france24fr.description: L'Arabie saoudite a bien failli créer l'exploit face à l'Uruguay lundi, au Mondial 2026. Les Faucons ont longtemps mené, puis ont résisté à la Celeste après l'égalisation, grâce à un gardien héroïque (1-1).

france24fr.title: Un bombardier B-52 américain s'écrase en Californie avec huit personnes à bord
france24fr.description: Au moins huit personnes sont présumées mortes après le crash, peu après son décollage lundi sur la base aérienne d'Edwards, en Californie, d'un bombardier américain B-52. Une enquête a été ouverte pour déterminer les causes de l'accident.

france24fr.title: Le G7 est-il encore influent aujourd’hui ?
france24fr.description: Certains des grands dirigeants du monde sont en France. Le sommet du G7 s'est ouvert ce lundi à Évian, en Haute-Savoie et il va durer trois jours jusqu'au 17 juin. Une question se pose alors : étant donné que le poids économique des pays du G7 a diminué avec la montée en puissance des économies émergentes, ce sommet a-t-il perdu de sa superbe ?

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Sabri Lamouchi limogé après la débâcle de la Tunisie contre la Suède, Hervé Renard nommé
france24fr.description: Le sélectionneur de la Tunisie Sabri Lamouchi a été démis de ses fonctions lundi et sera remplacé pour le reste de la Coupe du monde par un autre technicien français, Hervé Renard, a annoncé le président de la Fédération tunisienne à la télévision publique. Ce séisme sur le banc tunisien intervient à la suite de la lourde défaite des Aigles de Carthage face à la Suède (5-1) lors de leur premier match du Mondial 2026.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : 782 cas confirmés d'Ebola et deux nouvelles zones affectées, MSF s'inquiète
france24fr.description: L'épidémie d'Ebola en RDC : MSF tire la sonnette d'alarme. L'ONG s'inquiète des « dangereuses lacunes » dans la réponse sanitaire alors que l'épidémie se diffuse plus rapidement que les capacités de réponse mises en œuvre sur le terrain. Notre envoyée spéciale à Bunia a pu se rendre dans un hôpital.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : comment la FIFA justifie les tribunes vides
france24fr.description: Les images de tribunes clairsemées lors du match qui a opposé la Corée du Sud à la République Tchèque en phase de poules du Mondial ont relancé la polémique sur les prix des billets jugés exorbitants. La FIFA s'est expliquée quant aux photos et aux vidéos de sièges vides, en se défendant de tout échec lié à sa billetterie.

france24fr.title: Avec l'accord Iran-Etats-Unis, soudaine détente sur les prix du pétrole
france24fr.description: A peine l'annonce d'un accord de paix a-t-elle eu lieu que les marchés ont respiré un grand coup. Les bourses ont toutes passées la séance dans le vert alors que le pétrole, WTI américain ou Brent de la mer du nord entamaient une chute de 5% environ, les plaçant aux alentours de 80 dollars le baril. Pour les marchés, échaudés par le record de 120 dollars le baril atteint en avril, c'est la détente; les entreprises de l'aéronautique ou de l'automobile ont vu leurs actions s'apprécier franchement.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la Belgique et l'Égypte se neutralisent au terme d'une rencontre animée
Mondial 2026 : la Belgique et l'Égypte se neutralisent au terme d'une rencontre intense
france24fr.description: La Belgique et l'Égypte n'ont pas réussi à se départager (1-1), lundi, lors du premier match du groupe G du Mondial 2026. Les Diables Rouges ont longtemps couru après le score face à des Pharaons réalistes, mais l'entrée de Lukaku a été décisive pour obtenir le point du nul.

zeit.title: Commerzbank: Bund lehnt Übernahmeangebot von UniCredit für Commerzbank ab
zeit.description: Als zweitgrößter Aktionär weist der Bund das Übernahmeangebot von der italienischen Bank UniCredit zurück. Grund dafür seien wirtschaftliche und inhaltliche Punkte.

zeit.description: Insgesamt 44 Prozent der Beschäftigten erhalten im Sommer Urlaubsgeld. Arbeitnehmer mit Tarifvertrag sind im Vorteil. Frauen profitieren seltener von der Sonderzahlung.

zeit.description: Andrea Nahles, die Chefin der Bundesagentur für Arbeit, sagt: KI werde alle Jobs verändern. Hier verrät sie, warum kein Abschluss immun ist – und wie man sich wappnet.

zeit.title: Belfast: Elon Musk kündigt rechtliche Schritte gegen das ZDF an
zeit.description: Im ZDF hieß es, dass Elon Musk zur Jagd auf Migranten aufgerufen habe. Der kündigt rechtliche Schritte an, der Sender nennt die Aussage unpräzise und missverständlich.

zeit.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Tunesien entlässt Nationaltrainer Sabri Lamouchi nach Auftaktpleite
zeit.description: Nach dem Debakel gegen Schweden tauscht Tunesien den Trainer aus. Schiedsrichter Evans muss nach seiner umstrittenen Handgeste keine Konsequenzen fürchten. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: Sozialwohnungen: Zahl der Sozialwohnungen erneut gesunken
zeit.description: 2025 sind trotz Gegenmaßnahmen rund 20.000 Sozialwohnungen weggefallen. Damit ist die Zahl solcher Wohnungen weiter gesunken. Besonders in NRW ist die Lücke groß.

zeit.title: Straßenverkehr: Mehrheit spricht sich für strengere Promillegrenzen aus
zeit.description: Fast die Hälfte aller Deutschen spricht sich in einer Umfrage für ein absolutes Alkoholverbot am Steuer aus. Für Radler und E-Biker gibt es mehr Promilletoleranz.

nzz.title: DATENANALYSE - Wie beliebt ist Donald Trump?
nzz.description: Täglich aktualisierte Umfragewerte zeigen, wie die Amerikaner derzeit zur Amtsführung ihres Präsidenten stehen. Eine Übersicht in Grafiken.

nzz.title: INTERAKTIV - Gas weiterhin doppelt so teuer wie vor der Krise – die aktuellen Zahlen zur Energieversorgung in Deutschland
nzz.description: Wie wirken sich Energiewende und globale Krisen auf Strom- und Gaspreise aus? Hier gibt es jeden Tag die aktuellen Zahlen.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - G-7-Gipfel in Évian: Das Programm des zweiten Tags +++ Selenski schlägt Treffen mit Putin vor
nzz.description: Von Montag bis Mittwoch empfängt Emmanuel Macron in Évian am Genfersee die Staats- und Regierungschefs der G-7. Frankreich und die Schweiz haben sich mit einem grossen Sicherheitsdispositiv auf Proteste vorbereitet. Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten im Ticker.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Fussball-WM 2026: Die Fifa straft das Handzeichen von Schiedsrichter Evans nicht +++ Kapverdischer Goalie erntet Follower
nzz.description: Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten zur Fussball-WM in Kanada, Mexiko und den USA.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Kultur: Jazzpianist Abdallah Ibrahim mit 91 Jahren gestorben
nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus dem Feuilleton.

nzz.title: Die Wirtschaftsprüfer geraten zunehmend in eine Vertrauenskrise: Auch KPMG stolpert über Datenlecks
nzz.description: Nach dem PwC-Skandal in Australien steht mit KPMG bereits der nächste Riese der Big Four unter Beschuss. Der Missbrauch von Daten erschüttert das Fundament der grossen Beratungskonzerne.

nzz.title: Wolfsgruss, Tauhid und «White Power»: Handzeichen und was sie bedeuten
nzz.description: Schon die alten Römer kannten den «digitus impudicus», den schamlosen Finger. Politische und religiöse Fingerzeige sorgen oft für Kontroversen. Ein Überblick.

nzz.title: Trumps Abkommen in Sicht: Ist Iran der heimliche Sieger?
nzz.description: Am Freitag will Trump in Genf ein Rahmenabkommen zwischen den USA und Iran unterzeichnen. Falls es dazu kommt, was für ein Friede entstünde da?

nzz.title: Das iranische Regime zeigt sich zufrieden – doch längst nicht alle Iraner sind mit dem jüngsten Abkommen einverstanden
nzz.description: In der Nacht auf Montag protestierten radikale Gruppen gegen die Rahmenvereinbarung mit den USA. Sie sehen darin einen Verrat an der Islamischen Revolution.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Krawalle am G-7-Gipfel: Macron lässt die braven Schweizer zahlen
nzz.description: Der französische Präsident hat die Anti-G-7-Demonstrationen geschickt in die Schweiz ausgelagert. An eine Kostenbeteiligung denkt er nicht. Die Schweizer übertreiben es mit ihren Guten Diensten.

nzz.title: Der stille Stratege: Philippe Stern, Patron der Genfer Uhrenmanufaktur Patek Philippe, ist gestorben
nzz.description: Philippe Stern führte Patek Philippe durch die Quarzkrise, baute ihre industrielle Basis aus und machte die Geschichte der Genfer Uhrenmanufaktur zum Teil des Geschäftsmodells. Nun ist er mit 87 Jahren gestorben.

nzz.title: Didier Deschamps, der Trainer, der sein Land vereint
nzz.description: Die WM in den USA ist für den französischen Nationaltrainer das letzte Turnier. Die Verdienste seiner langen Ära verdeutlicht nichts so gut wie die jüngste Skandal-Doku über die französische Blamage an der WM 2010.

nzz.title: Neue Anklage gegen René Benko: Es geht um Betrug und ein wertvolles Jagdgewehr
nzz.description: Der gefallene Immobilienmogul muss sich in einem dritten Prozess verantworten, in dem es erstmals um sein Geschäftsgebaren kurz vor der Signa-Pleite geht. Bald könnte zudem das erste rechtskräftige Urteil erfolgen.

nzz.title: Die EU-Beitritts-Verhandlungen mit der Ukraine gehen nun richtig los – aber Kiew sollte sich nicht zu früh freuen
nzz.description: Die neue ungarische Regierung hat das Veto gegen die Eröffnung von Verhandlungskapiteln aufgegeben. Die Stärken der Ukraine sind gleichzeitig ihr Problem.

nzz.title: Trotz Frieden mit Iran: Das Öl vom Persischen Golf wird auf sich warten lassen
nzz.description: Die Strasse von Hormuz soll nach über hundert Tagen Iran-Krieg wieder geöffnet werden. Die Folgen werden noch ebenso lange zu spüren sein. Antworten auf die wichtigsten Fragen.

nzz.title: Nach der 10-Millionen-Abstimmung: Thomas Aeschi fordert Minderheitenschutz für konservative Deutschschweizer
nzz.description: Der Chef der SVP-Bundeshausfraktion Thomas Aeschi zieht mit einer gewagten Aussage den Zorn der Westschweiz auf sich. Politisch nimmt er FDP und Mitte in die Pflicht – in einem Punkt aber spannt er mit der SP zusammen.

observador.title: Morreram 57 pessoas afogadas este ano
observador.description: Coimbra, Braga e ilha da Madeira destacam-se com o maior número de afogamentos desde o início do ano, com os valores mais elevados desde 2017. Rios e mar continuam a ser zonas de risco.

observador.title: EUA-Irão: trégua para preparar a paz ou uma nova guerra?
observador.description: A trégua dá tempo a Trump e ao Irão. O presidente dos EUA garante petróleo e o Estreito de Ormuz livre. Mas apesar de celebrada, todos sabem que a guerra pode voltar a qualquer momento.

observador.title: Tribunal recusa saída da prisão do filho de Mette-Marit
observador.description: Ministério Público recorreu da decisão que permitia que Høiby, condenado a quatro anos de prisão, acompanhasse a mãe, princesa herdeira norueguesa, que está à espera de um transplante do pulmão.

observador.title: Mundial: Portugal foca-se no bronze e no mergulho tático
observador.description: Enquanto a bola não rola, o plano é duro: molhar o pé para "adaptar à humidade". Entre mergulhos e o físico real do Ronaldo, a malta prepara-se para brilhar... ou para bronzear.

observador.title: Banco do Japão sobe juros para nível mais alto em 31 anos
observador.description: Japão aumenta a taxa de juro de referência para 1%, um valor que não se via desde 1995. Banco central está mais preocupado com o impacto da guerra na inflação do que no crescimento.

observador.title: “Muitos não sabem que o Padrão foi para a sucata em 1943”
observador.description: Seduzida por Portugal (“os portugueses não são frios, são tímidos”), Ellen Sapega logo que se reformou veio preparar a exposição “Padrão. Casa - Obsessão”, e diz: “Descobri Lisboa pelos transportes”

observador.title: 8h. Zelensky marca hoje presença na cimeira do G7
observador.description: Expectativa para saber se há ou não encontro privado entre Zelensky e Trump. Ainda, no dia antes da estreia de Portugal no Mundial, o plantel tem hoje uma agenda preenchida.

observador.title: Um Mundial entre tubarões e azuis e deputados
observador.description: Cabo Verde estreou-se na competição com um empate contra a Espanha; a FPF convidou líderes parlamentares para ver Portugal (e há exceções na lei); em Ormuz, o trânsito será difícil de retomar.

observador.title: Cabo Verde trava Espanha e Vozinha brilha no Mundial
observador.description: Cabo Verde travou a Espanha num jogo épico. O herói foi Vozinha, o guarda-redes de 40 anos que brilhou em campo e já soma 5,6 milhões de seguidores no Instagram.

observador.title: Nintendo. Exemplar do Super Mario Bros vendido por 3 milhões
observador.description: Na sexta-feira foi vendida uma cópia do videojogo Super Mario Bros para a consola NES com o cobiçado selo de etiqueta brilhante, sendo a atual cópia de videojogo mais valorizada atualmente.

observador.title: A noite em que o futebol saiu da sombra dos simbolismos
observador.description: Durante 90 minutos, as seleções foram responsáveis por fazer esquecer, com sucesso, toda a tensão vivida fora do campo. O jogo acabou em empate (2-2), mas houve um claro vencedor: o futebol.

observador.title: Trump faz 80 anos com bolo, telefonemas e... luta
observador.description: Donald Trump celebrou os 80 anos com combates e "ringues" diplomáticos. Já Bruce Springsteen, resolveu limpar a alma e pedir desculpa a Bono por um "não" com duas décadas.

observador.title: EUA-Irão. "Pode baixar o preço dos combustíveis"
observador.description: Francisco Pereira Coutinho diz que pacto EUA-Irão pode vir a baixar os preços do combustível. O especialista em direito internacional acredita que é expectável um "conflito congelado" para a Ucrânia.

observador.title: Justiça falhou no caso de Odair?
observador.description: Tribunal condena agente da PSP a pena suspensa por excesso de legítima defesa. Já André Ventura tenta forçar o Governo a ceder em medidas que ameaçam a sustentabilidade da Segurança Social.

observador.title: Assobios, o sol e o leão: a estreia do Irão no Mundial
observador.description: Em Los Angeles, não foi "só futebol". Manifestações, batalha judicial sobre uma bandeira, assobios durante hino e uma conferência de imprensa sem uma pergunta sobre futebol. Tudo acabou num empate.

observador.title: Trânsito no Estreito de Ormuz levará "semanas" a normalizar
observador.description: Responsável pela maior operadora mundial no transporte marítimo de petróleo avisa que muitas empresas vão continuar a evitar a travessia do estreito, apesar do acordo que prevê a reabertura.

observador.title: Japão pede explicações aos EUA após restrições a IA
observador.description: Com Altman em Tóquio, a ministra das Finanças do Japão pediu explicações a Washington sobre a suspensão da Anthropic, decretada por motivos de segurança nacional, que afetou clientes em todo o mundo.

observador.title: 7h. Convites da FPF aos deputados dispensam autorização
observador.description: Os líderes das bancadas e líderes partidários escapam ao limite dos 150 euros estabelecido como teto máximo para ofertas aos deputados. Ainda, portugueses preocupados com desinformação.

letemps.description:
Attendu mardi au sommet du G7, le président ukrainien participera à une réunion de travail consacrée à la paix et la sécurité pour l'Ukraine et l'Europe. Il a proposé, la veille, de rencontrer son homologue russe aux Etats-Unis, lors d’un appel téléphonique avec Donald Trump. Notre suivi

letemps.description:
Le thème de la souveraineté numérique est de plus en plus présent en Suisse, des spécialistes redoutant une trop forte dépendance aux solutions américaines. Mais il manque encore une volonté claire émanant du Conseil fédéral

letemps.description:
La justice française doit se prononcer sur sa capacité à juger l’affaire Tran To Nga, qui oppose une Franco-Vietnamienne de 84 ans à 14 firmes agrochimiques américaines accusées d’avoir fourni de l’«agent orange» à l’armée américaine pendant la guerre du Vietnam. letemps.description:
Ce mardi, le Conseil national discute de l’inversement du fardeau de la preuve pour lutter contre le blanchiment d’argent. Une ligne rouge pour certains avocats, qui craignent pour la présomption d’innocence. De son côté, la conseillère nationale PVL Céline Weber défend une justice plus efficace

letemps.title: En direct, Moyen-Orient – Le cadre d'accord a été signé par l'Iran et les Etats-Unis
letemps.description:
Le texte a été signé électroniquement par Donald Trump, J. D. Vance et le négociateur iranien Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, en amont d'une cérémonie vendredi à Genève. Selon le médiateur pakistanais, il doit mettre fin «de façon immédiate et permanente» à la guerre au Moyen-Orient sur tous les fronts et entraîner la réouverture du détroit d'Ormuz. Notre suivi

letemps.description:
La Coupe du monde aux Etats-Unis est l’occasion pour certains Américains d’ascendance helvétique de se connecter à leurs racines. Mais pour ce jeune étudiant rencontré au lendemain de Suisse-Qatar, c’est beaucoup plus que ça

letemps.title: Faut-il vraiment prendre des compléments alimentaires à la ménopause?
letemps.description:
Ce profond bouleversement hormonal peut entraîner chez les femmes des effets secondaires difficiles à vivre. Pour répondre à ce problème, l’industrie du complément alimentaire a développé une offre pléthorique, aux résultats très variables

spiegel.title: Capri-Sun-Chef hält Strohhalm-Petition für »schlecht gemacht«
spiegel.description: Mit Unterschriften von einer Million Kunden wollte Capri-Sun die Rückkehr des Plastikstrohhalms erkämpfen. Nicht mal ein Fünftel machte mit, nun räumt der Chef des Getränkeherstellers den Misserfolg ein.

spiegel.title: Gentechnik im Supermarkt: Warum das neue EU-Gesetz Probleme schafft - Meinung
spiegel.description: Bald könnte es mehr gentechnisch veränderte Lebensmittel in deutschen Supermärkten geben. Die EU-Reform ist gefährlich – aber nicht aus den Gründen, über die gestritten wird.

spiegel.title: Möglicher Irandeal und Straße von Hormus: Bis sich der Schiffsverkehr normalisiert, könnte es Wochen dauern
spiegel.description: Angesichts der vorläufigen Einigung mit Iran sprechen die USA bereits von einer vollständigen Öffnung der Straße von Hormus ab Freitag. Selbst wenn das gelingt, dürften die Lieferketten noch angespannt bleiben.

spiegel.title: Dortmund: Feuerwehr rettet vierjähriges Kind aus Dachrinne im vierten Stock
spiegel.description: Es kletterte offenbar unbemerkt aus dem Fenster: In Dortmund haben Einsatzkräfte ein Kind von einem Dach geholt. Die Feuerwehr spricht von einer »lebensgefährlichen Situation«.

spiegel.title: Urlaubsgeld: Wer leer ausgeht – und wer bis zu 3000 Euro erhält
spiegel.description: Manche bekommen fast 3000 Euro, andere eher ein Trinkgeld – und mehr als jeder Zweite gar nichts: Beim Urlaubsgeld gibt es riesige Unterschiede. Wer die besten Chancen auf den Gehaltszuschuss hat.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: Sheryl Crow kritisiert Käfigkämpfe zum 80. Geburtstag als »schändlich«
spiegel.description: Ein Wettkampf im Ultimate Fighting, der mit einem »abscheulichen und rassistischen Kommentar« endet: Sheryl Crow hat sich empört über Trumps Geburtstagsveranstaltung geäußert. Sie beließ es nicht bei Kritik an dem Event.

spiegel.title: Polen: Russischer Künstler und Putin-Kritiker Semyon Skrepetsky erschossen
spiegel.description: Er war für satirische Porträts von Kremlchef Putin und dem belarussischen Machthaber Lukaschenko bekannt. Jetzt wurde der russische Künstler Semyon Skrepetsky laut übereinstimmenden Berichten in Polen erschossen.

spiegel.title: Pflegereform: Sollen Kinder künftig für die Pflege ihrer Eltern zahlen?
spiegel.description: Weniger Schonvermögen und Zugriff auf Omas Häuschen: Zuletzt haben Unionspolitiker harte Sparvorschläge für Pflege und Gesundheit gemacht. Emmi Zeulner von der CSU gibt Kontra.

spiegel.title: Hannover: Polizisten wegen Vorwürfen der Körperverletzung und der Strafvereitelung im Amt suspendiert
spiegel.description: Gegen vier Beamte und eine Beamtin der Polizeidirektion Hannover laufen strafrechtliche Ermittlungen. Auch gegen zwei weitere Polizisten gibt es Vorwürfe. Die Polizeipräsidentin spricht von beschädigtem Vertrauen.

spiegel.title: »Ich musste vor Gericht dafür kämpfen, dass ich mein Kind in zusammenhängenden Zeitabschnitten sehen darf«
spiegel.description: Die Emotionen anderer zu zeigen, gehört zu seinem Job. Eine Rolle brachte Christoph Letkowski besonders an seine Grenzen – als Schauspieler und als Vater.

spiegel.title: Studieren in Koblenz: Campus, Wohnviertel, WG-Zimmer-Preise, Kneipen
spiegel.description: Zwischen Mosel und Rhein hat Sebastian Heinz nicht nur einen einzigartigen Studiengang gefunden, sondern auch eine Stadt voller kleiner Communitys. Warum Koblenz für ihn mehr ist als eine Durchgangsstation.

spiegel.title: Alle reden über »Yesteryear«. Muss man den Tradwife-Roman wirklich lesen?
News: Emmanuel Macron, Donald Trump, Wolodymyr Selenskyj, Friedrich Merz, Benjamin Netanyahu, Alexander Dobrindt
spiegel.description: Gastgeber Macron umwirbt den US-Präsidenten beim G7-Gipfel in Évian-les-Bains. Netanyahu ist der Verlierer des Irankriegs. Und Dobrindt weiht ein Zentrum gegen hybride Bedrohungen ein. Das ist die Lage am Dienstagmorgen.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 News heute: Iran muss die USA nach Auftaktspiel verlassen – Mehdi Taremi kritisiert Fifa
spiegel.description: Irans Nationalmannschaft muss nach dem WM-Auftakt in Los Angeles noch am Abend die USA verlassen. So sagt es Kapitän Mehdi Taremi. »Die Fifa sollte uns mehr helfen.« Alles Wichtige zur WM.

spiegel.title: »Ninja Warrior«-Athleten: Das große Hangeln – so werden Sie fit
spiegel.description: Viel Kraft, Ausdauer und Bewegungsgefühl brauchen »Ninja Warrior«-Athleten. Ein Gesicht der TV-Show ist Moritz Hans. Unser Autor hat ihn in der Kletterhalle getroffen: ein hartes Training an der Himmelsleiter und der Steilwand.

spiegel.title: Japanese Walking: So gelingt der perfekte Intervall-Spaziergang
spiegel.description: Noch immer fällt es vielen Menschen schwer, sich regelmäßig zu bewegen. Intervall-Spaziergänge könnten die Lösung sein. Warum der Fitnesstrend so effektiv ist und wie er bei der Gewichtsreduktion hilft.

spiegel.title: Iran-Krieg: Ölreserve der USA fällt auf tiefsten Stand seit 40 Jahren
spiegel.description: Der Krieg gegen Iran hat auch in den USA die Benzinpreise massiv steigen lassen. Als Reaktion hat die Trump-Regierung die Notfallreserven angezapft. Und die nähern sich nun einer riskanten Marke.

spiegel.title: Lukaschenko ruft Russland und Ukraine zu Kompromissen auf
spiegel.description: Belarus gilt als enger Verbündeter Moskaus. Nun rät Machthaber Alexander Lukaschenko Russland und der Ukraine zu Zugeständnissen, um den Krieg zu beenden. Ein militärischer Sieg sei für beide Seiten unrealistisch.

elpais.title: Todas las selecciones del Mundial 2026 en Estados Unidos, Canadá y México
elpais.description: La competición con más equipos de la historia pone en juego a 48 combinados nacionales durante cinco semanas. Consulte aquí todos los detalles

elpais.title: La guerra entre Von der Leyen y Kallas socava la frágil diplomacia de la Unión Europea
elpais.description: El pulso por las competencias entre la presidenta de la Comisión Europea y la alta representante para Política Exterior amenaza con minar la posición europea en un momento convulso para Europa

elpais.title: El fin de la guerra margina a Netanyahu
elpais.description: El pacto no cumple uno solo de los objetivos de Israel. El primer ministro acaba enemistado con Trump y sin logros que vender a su población a cuatro meses de las elecciones

elpais.title: Trump negocia un acuerdo nuclear similar al que rompió en 2018 y con un Irán en posición de más fuerza
elpais.description: El anterior pacto recogía garantías similares a las que se cree se discutirán ahora, en un contexto político mucho más desfavorable para el entendimiento

elpais.title: La izquierda recurre a los tribunales contra el proyecto de Ayuso de condicionar al padrón el acceso a la tarjeta de transportes
elpais.description: IU solicitará la suspensión cautelar, el Gobierno de España y Más Madrid estudian medidas legales, y Renfe protesta, mientras que Vox aplaude

elpais.title: El Hospital de Torrejón pide a la Comunidad de Madrid no recibir nuevos médicos residentes como medida de ahorro
elpais.description: La petición llega después de que el CEO de la empresa gestora, Ribera Salud, dijera en su polémico audio publicado por EL PAÍS que los salarios de los MIR suponen “cinco o seis millones que nos hacen falta”

elpais.title: ¿Por qué los mismos cereales son buenos en España y se desaconsejan en otros países?
elpais.description: La nutricionista Azahara Nieto analiza los fallos de Nutri-score frente a otras etiquetas más precisas que se usan en Chile o Colombia

elpais.title: Prioridad regional
elpais.description: Además de xenófoba, la medida que quiere plantar la Comunidad de Madrid en materia de transporte demuestra un profundo desprecio por lo público, que pasa a concebirse como algo fragmentario y excluyente

elpais.title: Una paradoja española
elpais.description: Los partidos tradicionales aguantan más que en otros países europeos cuyas ciudadanías están igual de hastiadas y son igual de críticas con la política

elpais.title: Mbappé, correr o no correr ante su debut en el Mundial
elpais.description: Francia se estrena ante Senegal con la duda de cómo encajará su capitán con los pujantes Olise, Doué y Dembélé en el sistema de un Deschamps que le protege

elpais.title: Cabo Verde pincha el globo de España
elpais.description: La selección de Luis de la Fuente, una de las grandes favoritas del campeonato, no consigue superar la resistencia del equipo africano, debutante, en un partido sin chispa de la Roja pese al regreso de Lamine

elpais.title: Una decepción de España, muchos pases y ningún gol
elpais.description: El empate de la selección en el Mundial frente a Cabo Verde deja el debut del equipo de Luis de la Fuente reducido a un partido lento, tenso y sin ocasiones

elpais.title: Arabia Saudí también le arranca un empate histórico a Uruguay y alivia a España
elpais.description: Un gol de Maxi Araujo a diez minutos del final evita un bochorno de época a los charrúas, que mejoraron en el segundo acto tras un primer tiempo plano

elpais.title: Competencia abre expediente a los seis grandes bancos españoles por la guerra hipotecaria
elpais.description: La CNMC investiga al Santander, BBVA, CaixaBank, Sabadell, Bankinter y Unicaja por desvelar detalles de su política comercial

elpais.title: Brasil acusa de homicidio y encarcela a los operarios que lanzaron a una mujer sin sujeción desde un puente
elpais.description: Los acusados no supieron explicar a la policía quién era la persona responsable de colocar la cuerda y verificar la seguridad antes del salto

elpais.title: El helicóptero en el que murieron Gaspi y Oliver Tree, investigado por irregularidades en 2024 en Brasil
elpais.description: La policía investiga las causas de la colisión en el aire en Río. Los pilotos y las aeronaves tenían los papeles en regla

elpais.title: Al menos ocho militares muertos al estrellarse un avión B-52 en California
elpais.description: El aparato acababa de despegar para un vuelo rutinario de prueba, según ha informado la Fuerza Aérea

elpais.title: La acusación liderada por Hazte Oír pide retirarle el pasaporte a Begoña Gómez
elpais.description: El defensa de la esposa de Sánchez denuncia en una vista preliminar que se ha “instrumentalizado” esta causa para atacar al Gobierno: “Quien quiera hacer política que vaya a la calle, no a un tribunal”

republika.title: G7 a Evian, le news di oggi. Zelensky arrivato a Ginevra: previsto bilaterale con Trump
republika.description: La prima sessione di lavoro del vertice incentrata sull’Ucraina. In arrivo leader di Egitto, Eau e Qatar

republika.title: Guerra in Iran, le news. Ft: “Usa valutano 300 miliardi a Teheran legato a obiettivi rispettati”
republika.description: Tre esplosioni a Hormuz dopo la firma digitale dell’accordo di pace. Macron nel bilaterale con Trump: “Pronti a dispiegare caccia, fregate e portaerei nello Stretto”. Il tycoon: “Un paio di navi francesi ci fanno comodo”

republika.title: Patrizia Reggiani, falso il testamento della madre: a lady Gucci eredità da 20 milioni
republika.description: Il tribunale milanese ha dichiarato falso l’atto con cui la 90enne Silvana Barbieri lasciava tutto a una fondazione costituita dal suo esecutore testamentario

republika.title: Argentina, niente alimenti ai figli: no al mondiale per 13.000. E c’è chi arriva in bici nel Kansas
republika.description: Il governo ha fornito agli Usa la lista nera dei genitori che hanno acquistato voli e biglietti per vedere l'Albiceleste, dimenticandosi di pagare gli alimenti. E poi c'è anche chi ha percorso 17mila km in bici in 9 mesi per arrivare fino a Kansas City

republika.title: Iran-Nuova Zelanda 2-2: inno di Teheran fischiato, a fine partita giocatori applauditi
republika.description: A Los Angeles l’esordio nel Mondiale americano degli asiatici il giorno dopo l’annuncio dell’accordo di pace in Medio Oriente. Tra i due gol di Just le reti di Razaeian e Mohebi. Il ct: “Siamo la squadra più maltrattata”

republika.title: L’arbitro Evans e il gesto del White Power: “Un tic, nessun messaggio". La Fifa archivia il caso
republika.description: La difesa dell’assistente Var di Germania-Curacao, accusato di aver ammiccato al suprematismo bianco: “Le immagini mostrano che l’ho ripetuto tante volte mentre tenevo una penna tra le dita”

republika.title: La pazienza non va al Mondiale
republika.description: La Tunisia ha esonerato Lamouchi dopo la sconfitta per 5-1 contro la Svezia nella prima partita del girone. La frenesia del calcio dei club sta colpendo anche le nazionali

republika.title: G7, l’Europa in campo. Macron: “Missione per Hormuz”, Trump: “Non serve molto aiuto”
republika.description: Al vertice di Evian il presidente Usa annuncia: “Venerdì riapre lo stretto senza pedaggi”. Sorrisi dopo il gelo con Parigi: “Emmanuel un amico speciale”. Il leader francese: passo fondamentale per la pace

republika.title: Cinque paesi e 12 navi per sminare lo stretto di Hormuz, sei mesi per le bonifiche
republika.description: Volenterosi pronti a partire ma c’è il nodo dei tempi lunghi. Bisognerà concordare con Teheran i termini dell’intervento

republika.title: G7, Meloni: “Siamo pronti” ma si attende lo scudo americano
republika.description: Il saluto con il tycoon a Evian dopo mesi di gelo. Per la missione nel Golfo due o tre cacciamine, una fregata e una nave logistica

republika.title: Via libera vincolato all’ok del Parlamento. Centrosinistra cauto
republika.description: Dopo la firma di Ginevra il cdm dovrà approvare una delibera. Il Pd: “Prima una vera pace”. Dubbi di M5S e Avs. Azione: “Sì se c’è l’Ue”

republika.title: La firma digitale e l’attesa per il vertice tra Vance e Ghalibaf
republika.description: Dati biometrici e certificati digitali per verificare l’identità della parti. Una volta chiuso, il documento viene crittografato e inserito in una procedura di controllo, che prevede la verifica delle identità, con data, ora della firma e posizione geografica dei firmatari

republika.title: Israele, Netanyahu sotto accusa. “Ma la nostra lotta non è finita”
republika.description: Le opposizioni all’attacco del premier: “Incapace di vincere”. Ma lui replica: “Ho salvato il mio Paese”. E lancia stoccate a Trump

republika.title: Da Hormuz al nucleare, la lunga serie di omissis nel memorandum
republika.description: L’intesa rinvia a trattative future la soluzione dei punti di dissidio all’origine della decisione di attaccare la Repubblica islamica

republika.title: Petraeus: “Trump vince solo se riuscirà a eliminare l’uranio iraniano già arricchito”
republika.description: L’ex capo della Cia: “I risultati concreti sono due: la revoca del blocco dello Stretto e la proroga del cessate il fuoco”

republika.title: In Iran l’ora dell’orgoglio, i generali gonfiano il petto: “Abbiamo sconfitto i nemici”
republika.description: Tra i leader politici prevale la cautela. Pezeshkian: “Vedremo dai negoziati”. Araghchi: “Per esperienza andiamo senza sfiducia”

republika.title: Il libro di Draghi: “L’Europa torni a crescere per difendere il suo sogno”
republika.description: “Competere o sparire” raccoglie i discorsi degli ultimi tre anni e la sua visione dell’Ue: “Garantire gli stessi diritti anche ai giovani e a chi non è ancora nato e tutelare la nostra libertà”

republika.title: Parte il negoziato per l’adesione dell’Ucraina all’Ue
republika.description: L’Unione apre il primo ciclo di trattative. Von der Leyen: “Passi avanti nelle riforme”

nyt.title: Potential End of War Tests Trump’s Promise of Quick Economic Rebound
nyt.description: Gas prices and other goods could remain elevated for months, adding to the political challenge facing the White House in the midterm elections.

nyt.title: Netanyahu Says Israel Will Keep Forces in Lebanon, Despite U.S.-Iran Deal
nyt.description: “The struggle has not ended,” a defiant Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told Israelis.

nyt.title: Naval Mines Could Still Stymie Gulf Shipping After War
nyt.description: The U.S. Navy will be deploying a new generation of drone-based countermeasures to search the sea floor and surface for any mines Iran laid.

nyt.title: Will Commercial Ships Have to Pay to Pass Through the Strait of Hormuz? Maybe.
nyt.description: Charging a toll is illegal under international law, but some fees are allowed for services. It is not clear what services Iran would provide, but there were no fees charged before the war.

nyt.title: Japan Raises Rates to 31-Year High to Ward Off War Inflation
nyt.description: Going against Prime Minister Takaichi’s wishes, Japan’s central bank acted amid U.S. pressure, a tanking currency and inflation from energy disruptions.

nyt.title: China’s Spending Slowdown Deepens as Households Tighten Their Belts
nyt.description: The unexpected decline in retail sales underscored China’s growing reliance on exports to sustain economic growth as domestic demand continues to falter.

nyt.title: Gov. Gavin Newsom Says Trump Is Investigating Him and His Wife
nyt.description: Aides to Gov. Gavin Newsom of California say several people associated with the couple have been contacted by federal agents in the past week. He criticized the move as politically motivated.

nyt.title: Algae Is Turning the Reflecting Pool Green. Again.
nyt.description: Algal blooms have hit the site, between the Lincoln Memorial and the Washington Monument, after a $14.2 million repair project.

nyt.title: Lawmakers Warn Trump Officials Not to Pursue Arch Project Without Congress
nyt.description: In a letter to Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and national parks officials, several Democrats and a Senate independent said that members of the administration could face fines and even criminal prosecution.

nyt.title: Kennedy Seeks to Expedite Appeal of Ruling That Blocked His Vaccine Policies
nyt.description: The health secretary is trying to restart the work of a panel that advises the government on vaccines, after a judge froze its decisions and prevented it from meeting.

nyt.title: Why Team Iran Is in a Tough Spot at the World Cup
nyt.description: At its first game in Los Angeles, the men’s national team drew spectators who weren’t coming for the soccer, but rather to protest the regime in Tehran.

nyt.title: How Kratom, an Addictive Gas Station Drug, Found Allies in Trump’s Cabinet
nyt.description: With support from Markwayne Mullin and Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the kratom industry is pursuing a potentially lucrative policy. Mr. Mullin owns equity in a company that could benefit.

nyt.title: How Quebec Left the Church and Became the World Leader in Assisted Dying
nyt.description: A society once strongly Roman Catholic has rejected the church’s prohibition on euthanasia, with many instead viewing control over one’s death as an individual right.

nyt.title: Montana Democrats Are Divided Over How to Win a Republican-held Senate Seat
nyt.description: A rift in Montana between the Democratic nominee and an independent candidate could boost Republican hopes of holding on to an open seat in conservative territory.

nyt.title: Dan Sullivan Namesake Is Disqualified From Alaska Senate Ballot
nyt.description: Republicans had accused Democrats of attempting to confuse voters by boosting a candidate with the same name as the incumbent Republican senator.

nyt.title: 8 Dead in B-52 Bomber Crash at Edwards Air Force Base in California
nyt.description: The aircraft burst into flames on Monday morning shortly after takeoff from Edwards Air Force Base in California, officials said. The cause is still under investigation.

nyt.title: A Knicks-Inspired Baby-Naming Boom Is Coming After Championship Win, Experts Say
nyt.description: Jalen Brunson could become the next Michael Jordan of baby names, but don’t expect more Victors or Wembys, the experts say.

nyt.title: How ‘The Furious’ Somersaults Through a Wild Action Scene
nyt.description: The new movie is packed with showstopping action, but one standout sequence has our hero rolling over a pyramid of henchmen. Here’s what it took.

npr.title: G7 leaders open summit talks in France on Ukraine and the Middle East
npr.description: The talks come on the heels of President Trump's announcement of an agreement to end the U.S. war against Iran. In recent weeks, the Iranian conflict has overshadowed the war in Ukraine.

npr.title: Trump arrives in France for G7 leaders summit, touting peace deal with Iran
npr.description: French president Emmanuel Macron met with Trump and congratulated him for signing the new Iran agreement.

npr.title: U.S. and Iran reach an agreement, but details remain scant
npr.description: President Trump says a deal had been reached to prolong a ceasefire with Iran and open the Strait of Hormuz, but many challenges remain.

npr.title: Drone strikes one of Ukraine's key Christian and cultural sites
npr.description: Russian strikes have left cultural scars across Ukraine, damaging Kharkiv's Art Museum and striking Kyiv's historic Pechersk Lavra monastery, reminding how war reaches even sacred and storied places.

npr.title: Crude oil is cheaper as markets embrace news of a U.S.-Iran deal
npr.description: Crude oil prices are falling as oil markets react to President Trump saying the U.S. and Iran have agreed on a framework for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

npr.title: Lead negotiator on 2015 Iran nuclear deal weighs in on what's next for Trump's deal
npr.description: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with Wendy Sherman, the lead U.S. negotiator on the 2015 Iran nuclear agreement, about the road ahead for U.S. negotiators aiming to strike a new deal to end the Iran war.

npr.title: Former American businessman detained in Myanmar after alleged financial misconduct
npr.description: Adam Castillo, founder of AGS Myanmar, was detained Thursday at Yangon International Airport. The U.S. State Department is aware of a reported detention but hasn't commented further.

npr.title: Trump announces deal to end war in Iran. And, how to stay safe in deadly heat
npr.description: Trump says a deal has been reached to end the war between the U.S. and Iran. Plus, this is what extreme temperatures do to the human body — and how you can keep yourself safe.

new-sci.description: We can no longer ignore the growing threat of fully autonomous weapons. The world must either act to ban them or accept that they are the future of war

new-sci.description: Global weather agencies have declared that El Niño has begun, and models show it is more likely than not to be a "super" El Niño. The climate pattern boosts extreme weather around the world, and could lead to record temperatures

phys-org.title: A new approach to the EU's promised cross-border climate action
phys-org.description: The EU must reduce its greenhouse gas emissions by 90% by 2040 relative to 1990—of which 5 percentage points can be achieved through climate action elsewhere, according to the 2025 law. A study by the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK) now proposes a novel instrument for this external component: performance-based Jurisdictional Reward Funds. This avoids perverse incentives, strengthens international and thus also European climate action, and costs just 5 billion euros annually.

phys-org.title: Online courses drive deeper learning when autonomy, social engagement and strong tasks connect
phys-org.description: Many people do not finish a massive open online course (MOOC). This does not match the goal of large-scale online learning. Learners have different goals and backgrounds. Xiaomei Wei's dissertation research looks at what keeps students engaged and what helps them learn the course content deeply in a MOOC. Wei will defend her dissertation on June 25 at Leiden University.

phys-org.title: Conflict hits schooling hardest where children are the target—study
phys-org.description: According to UNESCO, around 250 million children (16%) globally are out of school, although they are of an age to be at school in their countries. Available evidence suggests that out-of-school numbers are extremely high in conflict-affected countries, though the exact number is hard to quantify. For example, in the Central African Republic, South Sudan and Eritrea, more than 50% of primary school-age children are not going to school.

phys-org.title: Venus' strange rotation was likely triggered by a high-velocity, moon-sized impactor
phys-org.description: Venus' bizarre and extraordinarily slow retrograde rotation on its axis has long puzzled planetary scientists. But in a new paper presented at the recent European Geosciences Union General Assembly in Vienna, the authors argue that their models indicate a high-angle, moon-sized, high-velocity impactor likely triggered Venus' strange 248-day rotation. And it probably happened within the first 50 million years of Venus' formation.

phys-org.title: Electron beam curing could unlock tougher, faster coatings for packaging and cars
phys-org.description: Coatings are everywhere. A thin protective layer, often barely visible. They keep out moisture, sunlight and rust, helping products last longer. Think of laminate on kitchen cabinets, automotive body coatings or the outer layer of a soda can or chip bag.

phys-org.title: Traditional legal systems are ill-equipped for the fast-moving realities of climate change, study warns
phys-org.description: Traditional legal systems around the world are increasingly ill-equipped to cope with the fast-moving impact of climate change on communities, new research warns. Courts and authorities that control planning and local services must follow rigid rules that are based on people's rights and environmental protection. However, changes to make laws more dynamic and responsive could help those who enforce them move beyond reacting to events and become more proactive as they manage urban spaces.

phys-org.title: Fungal highways are vast, yet hidden underground—new study
phys-org.description: Beneath our feet lie some of the largest living organisms on Earth. Fungi are mostly invisible and largely overlooked, but they help sustain the ecosystems and food systems that we depend on every day.

phys-org.title: Children learn life lessons from movies like Moana
phys-org.description: Children not only enjoy watching movies like Moana, but also learn lessons from them and apply those lessons to their own lives. That is the conclusion reached by communication scientists at Radboud University. For example, a movie can inspire children not to give up, to work together and to develop their own identity. In addition, movies can encourage children to think about social issues such as climate change and beauty standards.

phys-org.title: Brazil catchment models reveal opposite climate impacts on Amazon and Cerrado soils
phys-org.description: A comparative modeling study of two Brazilian rain catchments suggests that climate change will have contrasting effects on future soil erosion in the Amazon and Cerrado. The findings have implications for land management in both biomes in the coming decades.

phys-org.title: How plants rush energy to injured tissues to help them heal
phys-org.description: A new study finds that plants respond to injury by actively redirecting sugars to damaged tissues, helping fuel the regeneration process. Using a fluorescent sensor to track sugar movement in living plants, researchers have discovered that wounds trigger a localized shift in energy transport, concentrating glucose around the injury site. phys-org.title: Bacteria reveal 'glue' protein that fastens antibiotic-resistant outer membrane to cell wall
phys-org.description: Researchers at the University of Notre Dame and collaborators have discovered a key process in how the outer membrane of gram-negative bacteria attaches to the cell wall, advancing the understanding of how these bacteria frequently develop resistance to antibiotics.

phys-org.title: Climate compensation isn't always enough for landowners
phys-org.description: At first glance, it looks like a simple calculation. The state offers compensation. The climate demands action. Low-lying soils must be restored as wetlands. Yet landowners hesitate. According to anthropologist and Ph.D. student Kasper Krabbe from the Department of Agroecology at Aarhus University, that is exactly where the misunderstanding begins.

phys-org.title: What early modern literature can teach us about neurodivergence
phys-org.description: Does it seem as though more people are coming out as neurodivergent these days?

phys-org.title: New imaging technique measures single scramblase proteins, revealing lipid transport rates
phys-org.description: A new single-protein analysis technique gives researchers an unprecedented ability to study proteins called scramblases, which have critical roles in biology. The development of the new technique, in a study led by investigators at Weill Cornell Medicine and Ruhr University Bochum in Germany, expands the toolkit available to cell biologists and biophysicists and could someday be useful in devising new strategies against multiple diseases.

phys-org.title: International surrogates recruited on social media face emotional control in Georgia's booming childbirth market
phys-org.description: Since 2022, Georgia's surrogacy industry has boomed, with oversubscribed clinics now recruiting women from across Central Asia via Instagram and TikTok. New research conducted at the University of Oxford's Centre on Migration, Policy and Society (COMPAS) provides unprecedented insight into the hidden systems of emotional control sustaining Georgia's transnational surrogacy market.

phys-org.title: Beyond frozen snapshots, protein 'breathing' comes into view with combined imaging methods
phys-org.description: Advances in structural biology have allowed scientists to determine molecular structures with atomic-level detail, sometimes yielding static snapshots that do not reflect the dynamism of proteins. phys-org.description: A child at a playground tries to climb, jump or negotiate with a peer, and the attempt does not work. They fall, get left out of a game or reach another impasse. Then they try again.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

proj-syn.title: India’s Unfinished Reform Agenda
proj-syn.description: Elevated oil prices, potentially strong El Niño conditions during the monsoon season, and the tariff-induced fragmentation of global trade are bearing down on the Indian economy and will likely be a drag on GDP growth. But these adverse conditions may be a blessing in disguise if they force India to complete its economic reform agenda.

proj-syn.title: The Middle East’s New Normal
proj-syn.description: The most likely outcome of the Iran war is not peace but an unsatisfying ceasefire that leaves the underlying issues unresolved. This will mean an uneasy equilibrium in which Gulf countries go their own way, US influence wanes, and the regional order remains unsettled.

proj-syn.title: No Bridge Over Healing Waters for the G7
proj-syn.description: The French G7 presidency’s focus on global imbalances is both welcome and problematic. While long-standing trade imbalances between the United States, Europe, and China are, if anything, becoming even more troublesome, the leaders’ summit in Évian-les-Bains will do nothing to address the problem.

proj-syn.title: Are Government Stakes the Key to AI Sovereignty?
proj-syn.description: At first glance, reports that the US and Chinese governments are both considering taking stakes in national AI champions would seem to suggest a convergence between the world’s two leading AI powers. But a closer look reveals stark differences in their underlying strategies.

proj-syn.title: From the American Revolution to Universal Suffrage
proj-syn.description: Britain’s attempt to crush the American Revolution exposed a constitutional crisis at the heart of its empire. One English statesman saw in it proof that only broader suffrage could check royal power, tame corruption, and ensure that imperial rule remained compatible with liberty.

proj-syn.title: Jefferson’s Revolutionary Language
proj-syn.description: Of the delegates who assembled in Philadelphia in 1776 for the Second Continental Congress, only Thomas Jefferson possessed the skill, knowledge, and linguistic gifts to make the Declaration of Independence an immortal text. He was the self-appointed conscience of America, and sensational imagery was his stock-in-trade.

proj-syn.title: The Declaration of the Enslaved
proj-syn.description: For African-Americans, the Declaration of Independence was nothing but a “thin veil to cover the crimes” of slavery, as Frederick Douglass put it. Inspired by Haiti’s Declaration of Independence, free and enslaved Black people in the US found themselves subverting America’s founding document to achieve their own emancipation.

proj-syn.title: Free-Market Capitalism Is Destroying US Democracy
proj-syn.description: Far from two sides of the same coin, free-market capitalism and democracy are fundamentally incompatible. The only way to restore US democracy is to transform the system, so that it compensates innovators but limits their market power, while ensuring that the benefits of economic progress are more equitably shared.

proj-syn.title: Canada’s Great Recalibration
proj-syn.description: The growing fusion of economics, security, and technology has altered the nature of 21st-century interdependence, and Canada has responded by being more intentional. Rather than automatically serving as an extension of US-centered systems, it is creating more options across a wider network of relationships.

proj-syn.title: From Jefferson to Nehru
proj-syn.description: The Declaration of Independence continues to challenge countries, including the US and India, to measure themselves against the ideals they profess. But in a century marked by rising inequality, an authoritarian resurgence, and the emergence of new forms of domination, measuring up will become only more difficult.

proj-syn.title: The Roots of Democratic Decline
proj-syn.description: Notwithstanding recent setbacks for illiberal, populist, and authoritarian leaders in some countries, good-governance groups and experts on democratic decline continue to document a disturbing global trend toward “autocratization.” What remains to be seen is whether enough voters will wake up to the threat.

proj-syn.title: The Standard of Independence
proj-syn.description: Although revolutions would surely have occurred had the United States never broken from Britain in 1776, the Declaration of Independence gave later anticolonial movements inspiration and the language to shape their own aspirations. It offered a universal blueprint, even as the US itself adopted the ethos of empire.

proj-syn.title: The Declaration of Independence Turns South
proj-syn.description: Whether they were agreeing or arguing, the new countries that emerged across the Americas after the American Revolution influenced each other. Together, they helped shape the global development of modern democracy and the social and political movements that have shaped it ever since.

proj-syn.title: Capitalism’s Creature
proj-syn.description: The American Dream, with its basis in Thomas Jefferson’s immortal words, was one of the most powerfully generative ideas ever conceived. But the economy and impersonal systems it helped to bring into being are now shaping society and its individual members, rather than the other way around.

proj-syn.title: What the Declaration Did and Did Not Say
proj-syn.description: The American founders’ understanding of political community was ethnically and racially restrictive in ways that Americans have since repudiated. But the Declaration of Independence’s underlying logic and treatment of rights and what it takes to secure them remains as cogent as it was 250 years ago.

proj-syn.title: Independence for Me, But Not for Thee
proj-syn.description: The Declaration of Independence spoke of all states as being "separate and equal," reflecting the founders' deference to the norms of international law and practice.
